cor-mlt-expanded.title: One regression on expanded data
cor-mlt-expanded.html: Let the slopes be common, 𝛃𝛃βr=β, and the data ungrouped (mi=1). Build an expanded data set with one row for each pair (i,r) with r≤min(yi,c−1), response 1{yi=r}, and regressors (er,−x(i)), where er is the rth coordinate vector of length c−1. Then an ordinary binary regression with link F−1 on the expanded data has, as a function of 𝛉𝛃(θ,β), the log-likelihood of the sequential model; the two fits, their standard errors and their tests coincide.

def-mlt-baseline.title: Baseline-category logit model
def-mlt-baseline.html:
Let Y1,…,Yn be independent with 𝛑Yi∼Mult(mi,πi), and let x(i)∈Rp be the ith row of a model matrix X whose first column is 1. The baseline-category logit model with baseline c is 𝛃log⁡πirπic=x(i)⊤βr,r=1,…,c−1,{#eq-mlt-baseline}

with unknown 𝛃𝛃β1,…,βc−1∈Rp. Equivalently, writing 𝛃βc=0, 𝛃𝛃πir=exp⁡(x(i)⊤βr)/∑s=1cexp⁡(x(i)⊤βs) for every r.

def-mlt-cumulative.title: Cumulative link model
def-mlt-cumulative.html:
Let G be a continuous, strictly increasing distribution function on R and let x(i) be a vector of p regressors without an intercept. The cumulative link model is 𝛃G−1(γir)=θr−x(i)⊤βr,r=1,…,c−1,{#eq-mlt-cumulative}

with cutpoints θ1,…,θc−1 and slope vectors 𝛃𝛃β1,…,βc−1. With G=Λ, the standard logistic distribution function Λ(z)=ez/(1+ez), @eq-mlt-cumulative is the cumulative logit model 𝛃log⁡P(Yi≤r∣x(i))P(Yi>r∣x(i))=θr−x(i)⊤βr; with G=Φ it is the cumulative probit model, and with G(z)=1−exp⁡(−ez) the cumulative complementary log-log model. The special case 𝛃𝛃𝛃β1=⋯=βc−1=β is the proportional odds model when G=Λ, and is the subject of Section 36.3.

def-mlt-sequential.title: Sequential model
def-mlt-sequential.html:
With 𝛑Yi∼Mult(mi,πi) as in @def-mlt-baseline, let δir=P(Yi=r∣Yi≥r, x(i)),r=1,…,c−1,{#eq-mlt-continuation}

be the continuation ratios, or discrete stopping probabilities. The sequential model with link F−1 is 𝛃δir=F(θr−x(i)⊤βr),r=1,…,c−1,{#eq-mlt-sequential}

for a continuous, strictly increasing distribution function F. With F=Λ and common slopes 𝛃𝛃βr=β it is the continuation-ratio logit model. The category probabilities are πir=δir∏s<r(1−δis)  (r<c),πic=∏s<c(1−δis).{#eq-mlt-sequential-probs}

eq-mlt-baseline.html: 𝛃log⁡πirπic=x(i)⊤βr,r=1,…,c−1,

eq-mlt-common-or.html: 𝛃odds(Y>r∣x2)odds(Y>r∣x1)=exp⁡{(x2−x1)⊤β},

eq-mlt-continuation.html: δir=P(Yi=r∣Yi≥r, x(i)),r=1,…,c−1,

eq-mlt-cumulative.html: 𝛃G−1(γir)=θr−x(i)⊤βr,r=1,…,c−1,

eq-mlt-cumulative-prob.html: γir=P(Yi≤r∣x(i))=πi1+⋯+πir,r=1,…,c−1,

eq-mlt-derivative.html: ∂πir∂xij=πir(βrj−∑s=1cπisβsj).

eq-mlt-expfam.html: 𝛈𝛈𝛈f(y)=h(y)exp⁡{y~⊤η−mb(η)},b(η)=log⁡(1+∑s=1c−1eηs),

eq-mlt-factorization.html: ∏r=1cπiryir=∏r=1c−1δiryir(1−δir)Ri,r+1.

eq-mlt-grouped-ph.html: 𝛃𝛃P(Yi>r∣x(i))=exp⁡{−eθre−x(i)⊤β}=[P(Y>r∣0)]exp⁡(−x(i)⊤β),

eq-mlt-inverse-link.html: πr=eηr1+∑s<ceηs (r<c),πc=11+∑s<ceηs,

eq-mlt-moments.html: 𝛈𝛑𝛈𝛑𝛑𝛑E(Y~)=m∇b(η)=mπ~,Cov(Y~)=m∇2b(η)=m(diag(π~)−π~π~⊤),

eq-mlt-po.html: 𝛃log⁡P(Yi≤r∣x(i))P(Yi>r∣x(i))=θr−x(i)⊤β,r=1,…,c−1.

eq-mlt-score-general.html: 𝛙𝛑𝛙u(ψ)=∑i=1nDi⊤Vi−1(y~i−miπ~i),J(ψ)=∑i=1nmiDi⊤Vi−1Di.

eq-mlt-sequential.html: 𝛃δir=F(θr−x(i)⊤βr),r=1,…,c−1,

eq-mlt-sequential-probs.html: πir=δir∏s<r(1−δis)  (r<c),πic=∏s<c(1−δis).

exm-mlt-mode.title: Choosing how to travel
exm-mlt-mode.html:
Two hundred and ten travellers on the Sydney–Melbourne corridor each chose one of four modes: air (58), train (63), bus (30) or car (59). The regressors are the household income in units of $10,000 and the size of the travelling party. Take car as the baseline. Fitting @def-mlt-baseline by Newton–Raphson from 𝛃β=0 takes 7 steps to full double precision, and gives the following coefficients, with standard errors from the inverse information in parentheses.

logit intercept income (per $10,000) party size
air vs car 0.9435 (0.5498) 0.0354 (0.1030) −0.6006 (0.1992)
train vs car 2.4938 (0.5357) −0.5731 (0.1184) −0.3098 (0.1956)
bus vs car 1.9780 (0.6717) −0.3033 (0.1322) −0.9404 (0.3245)

Income does not distinguish air from car (z=0.34) but moves people strongly away from the ground alternatives: each extra $10,000 of household income multiplies the odds of train rather than car by e−0.5731=0.5638. Read through @prp-mlt-invariance, the same fit raises the odds of air over train by e0.6085 per $10,000. Party size pushes travellers towards the car, most sharply away from the bus. The likelihood ratio statistic against the intercept-only model is 2(−253.3408+283.7588)=60.836 on six degrees of freedom.

exm-mlt-po-check.title: The proportional odds model does not hold
exm-mlt-po-check.title_html: The proportional odds model does not hold
exm-mlt-po-check.html:
The common odds ratio of @thm-mlt-proportional-odds(d) is worth having only if it is there. For @exm-mlt-selfplacement, let all three slopes vary across the six cuts. The score statistic of @prp-mlt-checks is 67.667 on 15 degrees of freedom, p=1.16×10−8; the likelihood ratio statistic against the fitted unrestricted model is 67.420, agreeing to within half a percent as @prp-mlt-checks(b) predicts. One regressor at a time, on c−2=5 degrees of freedom:

regressor score statistic p likelihood ratio
age 17.542 3.58×10−3 18.367
education 41.258 8.32×10−8 40.190
income 20.056 1.22×10−3 20.155

Education is the main offender. Figure 36.3.1 shows why: its slope is near −0.3 at the three lowest cuts, near 0 at cuts 4 and 5, and back near −0.3 at cut 6. Education sharply separates the liberal end of the scale from everything above it, says almost nothing about position within the upper middle, and then separates the extreme conservative category again. That is a fact about the data, and a single number cannot express it.

exm-mlt-selfplacement.title: A seven-point scale
exm-mlt-selfplacement.html:
The 1996 American National Election Study asked 944 respondents to place themselves on a seven-point scale from extremely liberal (1) to extremely conservative (7); the counts are 16, 103, 147, 256, 170, 218 and 34. With the respondent’s age in decades, a seven-point education scale and a twenty-four-point household income scale as regressors, Fisher scoring for the common-slope cumulative logit model converges in 11 steps to

age (decades) education income
β^ 0.0942 −0.1249 0.0276
standard error 0.0357 0.0395 0.0104
z 2.637 −3.166 2.641

with cutpoints θ^=(−3.7744,−1.6378,−0.6159,0.5580,1.3625,3.6442), in order as @prp-mlt-ordering requires, and maximized log-likelihood −1613.8558. Older and richer respondents place themselves further to the right, more educated respondents further to the left: each decade of age multiplies the odds of a higher placement by 1.0988, each step up the education scale by 0.8826. Whether one should believe a single common slope is the question of Section 36.3, and for these data the answer turns out to be no.

exm-mlt-sequential-anes.title: Self-placement, fitted sequentially
exm-mlt-sequential-anes.html:
The self-placement data of @exm-mlt-selfplacement are not a stage process — nobody becomes extremely conservative by first passing through “extremely liberal” — but the sequential model is still a parameterization of the seven category probabilities, and comparing the fits shows what each family buys.

The at-risk counts are 944, 928, 825, 678, 422 and 252, and the expanded data set has 4049 rows. One binary logistic regression on it, as in @cor-mlt-expanded, gives cutpoints (−3.9705,−1.9870,−1.4252,−0.3784,−0.2744,1.9824) and slopes 0.0454 (age, per decade), −0.0866 (education) and 0.0174 (income), with standard errors 0.0270, 0.0303 and 0.0079. The signs agree with the proportional odds fit and the magnitudes are smaller, as one should expect: these are effects on a single stage transition, not on the whole scale. The multinomial log-likelihood is −1618.2981, which the script confirms equals the log-likelihood the binary regression reports — @thm-mlt-factorization to machine precision.

Akaike’s criterion is 3254.60 for the sequential model against 3245.71 for proportional odds (@def-sel-aic-bic): with nine parameters each, the cumulative model describes these data better, as a scale of opinion rather than a ladder of stages should. Letting every stage have its own slopes raises the log-likelihood to −1578.3794 and lowers the criterion to 3204.76, just below the unrestricted cumulative model’s 3208.29. Once the common-slope restriction goes, the two families have the same (c−1)(1+p) parameters and fit these data about equally well.

exm-mlt-sequential-simulation.title: When the mechanism really is sequential
exm-mlt-sequential-simulation.title_html: When the mechanism really is sequential
exm-mlt-sequential-simulation.html:
Generate 4000 observations from a four-stage sequential logit model with one standard normal regressor, cutpoints (−0.6,0,0.5) and slope β=1; the category counts come out as 1487, 1094, 693 and 726. The sequential fit recovers the slope as 0.9761, standard error 0.0309. The proportional odds fit of the same data, with the same number of parameters, returns 1.1352, which is not estimating β at all, and Akaike’s criterion is 9444.56 against 9515.66. A gap of seventy is not a close call.

The moral is not that one family is better — reverse the simulation and the verdict reverses with it — but that the choice is a modelling decision about how the response came about, on which the data have plenty to say.

exr-mlt-adjacent.title: C1
exr-mlt-adjacent.html: The adjacent-category logit model for an ordered response specifies 𝛃log⁡(πi,r+1/πir)=θr+x(i)⊤β for r=1,…,c−1, with x(i) not containing an intercept. Show that it is the baseline-category model @def-mlt-baseline with slope vectors 𝛃𝛃βr=(c−r)β∗ for a single vector 𝛃β∗, plus a free intercept for each r: a submodel obtained by (c−2)p linear restrictions, fitted with the same software after recoding the model matrix.

exr-mlt-collapse-fit.title: B3
exr-mlt-collapse-fit.html: Refit @exm-mlt-selfplacement after collapsing the seven categories into three (1–3, 4, 5–7) and again after dichotomizing at the middle category. Compare the three sets of slopes and their standard errors, and say which comparison is a check on the model and which is a statement about information.

exr-mlt-collapse-numeric.title: B1
exr-mlt-collapse-numeric.html: Using @thm-mlt-proportional-odds(b), predict what happens to the estimated slopes when the seven categories of @exm-mlt-selfplacement are collapsed to three, and compare with the actual refit in @exr-mlt-collapse-fit. Does the comparison support or undermine the proportional odds assumption here?

exr-mlt-count-parameters.title: A1
exr-mlt-count-parameters.html: A response has c=5 categories and the model matrix has p=4 columns including the intercept. How many free coefficients has the baseline-category logit model? How many has the saturated model for n ungrouped observations? How many degrees of freedom does the test that one regressor may be dropped have?

exr-mlt-iia.title: C2
exr-mlt-iia.html: Show that in @def-mlt-baseline the ratio πir/πir′ does not involve any third category — the independence of irrelevant alternatives. Construct a three-category example in which this is substantively absurd, and say what the assumption forces about the fitted probabilities when a new category is added that is nearly a copy of an existing one.

exr-mlt-information-singular.title: B2
exr-mlt-information-singular.html: Show directly that the c×c matrix 𝛑𝛑𝛑𝛑Σ(π)=diag(π)−ππ⊤ is nonnegative definite with Σ1=0, and that its restriction to the first c−1 coordinates is positive definite when every πr>0.

exr-mlt-interval-censored.title: C1
exr-mlt-interval-censored.html: Suppose an underlying continuous response Ui follows the linear model 𝛃Ui=x(i)⊤β+εi with εi having distribution function G, but Ui is recorded only as the interval (θr−1,θr] it falls in, with known cutpoints. Write down the log-likelihood, show it is the cumulative link model with the cutpoints held fixed, and say what is gained by knowing them (@exr-mlt-latent-scale).

exr-mlt-latent-scale.title: B2
exr-mlt-latent-scale.html: The cumulative logit model is unchanged if the latent scale is multiplied by a positive constant a and shifted by b, provided θr↦aθr+b and 𝛃𝛃β↦aβ. Deduce that only ratios of coefficients, and the standardized distances between cutpoints, are free of the arbitrary scale — and that a coefficient from a logit fit is not comparable with a coefficient from a probit fit without rescaling by roughly 1.8, the standard deviation of the logistic distribution.

exr-mlt-order-free.title: B1
exr-mlt-order-free.html: Show that in the proportional odds model the maximum likelihood estimate automatically satisfies θ^1<⋯<θ^c−1, provided every category is observed, so the ordering constraint never binds. (Hint: what is the likelihood if two cutpoints coincide or cross?)

exr-mlt-pairwise.title: B1
exr-mlt-pairwise.html: From the fitted coefficients of @exm-mlt-mode, compute the estimated log odds ratio of bus against train per $10,000 of income, and the estimated odds ratio of air against bus per extra person in the party. State which of these depend on the choice of baseline.

exr-mlt-po-df.title: A1
exr-mlt-po-df.html: A proportional odds model has c=4 and p=3. How many parameters does it have? How many does the model with cut-specific slopes have, and what are the degrees of freedom of the score test of @prp-mlt-checks with A={1,2,3} and with A={2}?

exr-mlt-po-interpret.title: A2
exr-mlt-po-interpret.html: In a proportional odds fit the coefficient of a treatment indicator is β^=0.7. Write down three correct sentences and one common incorrect one.

exr-mlt-po-monotone.title: C1
exr-mlt-po-monotone.html: Show that if the proportional odds model holds and βj>0, then E{h(Y)∣x} is increasing in xj for every nondecreasing function h. Deduce that the sign of βj is a statement that survives any recoding of the categories into numbers, as long as the recoding respects the order.

exr-mlt-po-rank.title: C2
exr-mlt-po-rank.html:
Let @thm-mlt-proportional-odds hold with a single binary regressor, let Y1 and Y2 be independent responses from the two groups, and let U1,U2 be the latent variables of part (a) of that theorem.

  1. Show that P(U2>U1)=E{Λ(β−ε)} with ε standard logistic, so that it is a function of β alone and strictly increasing in it.

  2. Show that the concordance probability of the observed responses, P(Y2>Y1)+12P(Y2=Y1), is increasing in β for fixed cutpoints. (Hint: write it as E{h(Y2)} for a nondecreasing h that depends only on the distribution of Y1.) Then evaluate it at β=1 for c=3 with cutpoints (−0.5,0.5) and again with (−3,3), and conclude that, unlike the odds ratio eβ, it is not free of the cutpoints.

  3. The sample version of (b) is the Mann–Whitney statistic divided by n1n2, with ties counted half. Say in what sense the proportional odds model is a regression version of the Wilcoxon–Mann–Whitney test, and in what sense it is not.

exr-mlt-po-scale.title: B2
exr-mlt-po-scale.html: Derive the cumulative logits of the scale-effect model 𝛃Ui=x(i)⊤β+σ(x(i))εi, 𝛄log⁡σ(x)=x⊤γ, with εi standard logistic. Show that it contains @eq-mlt-po as the case 𝛄γ=0, and that its cumulative logits never cross as functions of x.

exr-mlt-reverse.title: A1
exr-mlt-reverse.html: Verify the claim that reversing the category order maps the cumulative logit model to itself with 𝛃β and the cutpoints negated, and find what it does to the complementary log-log model.

exr-mlt-seq-collapse.title: C2
exr-mlt-seq-collapse.html: Does the sequential model have a collapsing invariance like @thm-mlt-proportional-odds(b)? Show that merging the last two categories leaves the model and the remaining parameters intact, but merging any other adjacent pair does not.

exr-mlt-seq-count.title: A1
exr-mlt-seq-count.html: How many parameters has the sequential model with common slopes? With stage-specific slopes? How many rows has the expanded data set of @cor-mlt-expanded when every subject falls in the last category?

exr-mlt-seq-discrete-survival.title: C1
exr-mlt-seq-discrete-survival.html: Let Ti be a discrete survival time taking values 1,2,…, possibly right-censored at a known time ci. Write the likelihood in terms of the discrete hazards λir=P(Ti=r∣Ti≥r), and show that it is again the expanded binary likelihood of @cor-mlt-expanded, now with subject-specific numbers of rows. What does censoring correspond to in @thm-mlt-factorization?

exr-mlt-seq-hazard.title: B1
exr-mlt-seq-hazard.html: Interpret δir as a discrete hazard and ∏s≤r(1−δis) as a survivor function. Show that under @prp-mlt-cloglog the model says 𝛃P(Yi>r∣x(i))=S0(r)exp⁡(−x(i)⊤β) for a baseline survivor function S0, and identify S0.

exr-mlt-seq-reverse.title: A2
exr-mlt-seq-reverse.html: Show by a three-category example that reversing the order of the categories changes the sequential model, but not the cumulative one (@exr-mlt-reverse).

lem-mlt-multinomial.title: The multinomial as an exponential family
lem-mlt-multinomial.title_html: The multinomial as an exponential family
lem-mlt-multinomial.html:
Let 𝛑Y∼Mult(m,π) with πr>0 for every r and ∑r=1cπr=1. Write Y~=(Y1,…,Yc−1)⊤ for the first c−1 counts and ηr=log⁡πrπc,r=1,…,c−1.

Then the probability mass function is 𝛈𝛈𝛈f(y)=h(y)exp⁡{y~⊤η−mb(η)},b(η)=log⁡(1+∑s=1c−1eηs),{#eq-mlt-expfam}

with h(y)=m!/(y1!⋯yc!). The map 𝛈𝛑η↦π is a bijection from Rc−1 onto the interior of the probability simplex, with inverse πr=eηr1+∑s<ceηs (r<c),πc=11+∑s<ceηs,{#eq-mlt-inverse-link}

and the first two moments are 𝛈𝛑𝛈𝛑𝛑𝛑E(Y~)=m∇b(η)=mπ~,Cov(Y~)=m∇2b(η)=m(diag(π~)−π~π~⊤),{#eq-mlt-moments}

where 𝛑π~=(π1,…,πc−1)⊤.

prp-mlt-checks.title: Testing and diagnosing the proportional odds restriction
prp-mlt-checks.title_html: Testing and diagnosing the proportional odds restriction
prp-mlt-checks.html:
Let A⊆{1,…,p} index the regressors whose slopes are allowed to vary, and embed @eq-mlt-po in the cumulative logit model 𝛃𝛅logitγir=θr−x(i)⊤(β+δr), where 𝛅δ1=0 and 𝛅δr is supported on A for r≥2. Write 𝛙𝛉𝛃𝛅ψ=(θ,β,δ) and let 𝛙ψ^0 be the maximum likelihood estimate under 𝛅δ=0. Then, under the regularity conditions recorded in Section 36.2 and if @eq-mlt-po holds:

  1. the score statistic 𝛙𝛙𝛙Ssc=u(ψ^0)⊤J(ψ^0)−1u(ψ^0), with u and J from @eq-mlt-score-general, is computable from the restricted fit alone, equals 𝛅𝛅𝛅𝛅uδ⊤[J−1]δδuδ, and converges in distribution to χ2 with (c−2)|A| degrees of freedom;

  2. the likelihood ratio and Wald statistics for the same hypothesis have the same limit and are asymptotically equivalent to Ssc;

  3. the c−1 separate binary logistic regressions of 1{Yi≤r} on x(i) estimate the same 𝛃β, so plotting their slopes with confidence intervals shows where any departure lies. The c−1 fits are dependent, so the plot is a diagnostic and not a test.

prp-mlt-cloglog.title: Sequential and cumulative complementary log-log models agree
prp-mlt-cloglog.title_html: Sequential and cumulative complementary log-log models agree
prp-mlt-cloglog.html:
Take F(z)=1−exp⁡(−ez) and common slopes. If the sequential model @eq-mlt-sequential holds with cutpoints θ~1,…,θ~c−1, then the cumulative complementary log-log model @eq-mlt-cumulative holds with the same 𝛃β and cutpoints θr=log⁡(∑s≤reθ~s),r=1,…,c−1,{#eq-mlt-laara}

which are automatically increasing. The map 𝛉𝛉θ~↦θ is a bijection onto the increasing sequences, so the two models are the same family, and the maximum likelihood fits agree.

prp-mlt-cumulative-score.title: Score and expected information for a smooth mean
prp-mlt-cumulative-score.title_html: Score and expected information for a smooth mean
prp-mlt-cumulative-score.html: Let 𝛑Yi∼Mult(mi,πi) independently, i=1,…,n, with 𝛑𝛑𝛙πi=πi(ψ) a smooth function of a parameter 𝛙ψ∈Rq and every πir>0. Write 𝛑π~i for the first c−1 probabilities, 𝛑𝛙Di=∂π~i/∂ψ⊤ and 𝛑𝛑𝛑Vi=diag(π~i)−π~iπ~i⊤. Then the score and the expected information are 𝛙𝛑𝛙u(ψ)=∑i=1nDi⊤Vi−1(y~i−miπ~i),J(ψ)=∑i=1nmiDi⊤Vi−1Di.{#eq-mlt-score-general}

prp-mlt-derivative.title: A coefficient is not a derivative of a probability
prp-mlt-derivative.title_html: A coefficient is not a derivative of a probability
prp-mlt-derivative.html:
In @def-mlt-baseline, with 𝛃βc=0 and xj a continuous regressor, ∂πir∂xij=πir(βrj−∑s=1cπisβsj).{#eq-mlt-derivative}

So the c derivatives sum to zero, the derivative for category r is positive exactly when βrj exceeds the probability-weighted average β¯j(x(i))=∑sπisβsj, and the baseline, whose coefficient is zero by construction, has a strictly positive derivative whenever β¯j(x(i))<0.

prp-mlt-invariance.title: Changing the baseline
prp-mlt-invariance.html:
Let 𝛃𝛃β^1,…,β^c−1 maximize the likelihood of @def-mlt-baseline, and set 𝛃β^c=0. Fix any s∈{1,…,c}. Then:

  1. for every pair of categories r,r′, 𝛃𝛃log⁡(πir/πir′)=x(i)⊤(βr−βr′); in particular a model with baseline s is the same model, with coefficients 𝛃𝛃𝛃βr(s)=βr−βs;

  2. refitting the model with baseline s gives 𝛃𝛃𝛃β^r(s)=β^r−β^s, the same maximized log-likelihood and the same fitted probabilities;

  3. the estimated covariance matrix of 𝛃β^(s) obtained from the refitted model equals 𝛃LCov^(β^)L⊤, where L is the linear map of (a); so standard errors of pairwise contrasts do not depend on which baseline was used.

prp-mlt-ordering.title: Cutpoints must stay in order
prp-mlt-ordering.html:
@eq-mlt-cumulative defines a probability distribution over the c categories at x(i) if and only if 𝛃𝛃𝛃θ1−x(i)⊤β1<θ2−x(i)⊤β2<⋯<θc−1−x(i)⊤βc−1.{#eq-mlt-ordering}

If the slopes are common, 𝛃𝛃βr=β for all r, this reduces to θ1<⋯<θc−1, a constraint on the parameters alone. If the slopes differ, the constraint involves x(i), and for any two cuts with 𝛃𝛃βr≠βr+1 there are values of x at which it fails.

thm-mlt-factorization.title: Factorization of the sequential likelihood
thm-mlt-factorization.html:
Let Rir=∑s≥ryis be the number of subjects at covariate pattern i still “at risk” at stage r, so that Ri1=mi and Rir=yir+Ri,r+1. Under @def-mlt-sequential, ∏r=1cπiryir=∏r=1c−1δiryir(1−δir)Ri,r+1.{#eq-mlt-factorization}

Consequently:

  1. the log-likelihood is ℓ=∑r=1c−1ℓr, where 𝛃ℓr(θr,βr)=∑i{yirlog⁡δir+Ri,r+1log⁡(1−δir)} is the log-likelihood of a binary regression with Rir trials and yir successes;

  2. if the parameters 𝛃(θr,βr) of different stages are unrestricted and distinct, the maximum likelihood estimate is obtained by c−1 separate binary regressions, one on the subjects at risk at each stage; the information matrix is block diagonal, and the estimates for different stages are asymptotically independent;

  3. Yir∣Rir∼Bin(Rir,δir), and these conditional distributions determine the multinomial law.

thm-mlt-proportional-odds.title: The proportional odds model
thm-mlt-proportional-odds.html:
Let 𝛃log⁡P(Yi≤r∣x(i))P(Yi>r∣x(i))=θr−x(i)⊤β,r=1,…,c−1.{#eq-mlt-po}

Then:

  1. (latent variable) @eq-mlt-po holds exactly when there is a latent response 𝛃Ui=x(i)⊤β+εi, with εi independent of x(i) and standard logistic, and Yi=r precisely when θr−1<Ui≤θr, where −∞=θ0<θ1<⋯<θc−1<θc=∞. Replacing the logistic distribution by any continuous, strictly increasing G gives the general cumulative link model of @def-mlt-cumulative with common slopes;

  2. (collapsing) let 0=a0<a1<⋯<ak=c be integers and define the coarsened response Yi∗=j when aj−1<Yi≤aj. Then Yi∗ follows the proportional odds model with the same 𝛃β and cutpoints θj∗=θaj, j=1,…,k−1. In particular dichotomizing at any cut r gives a binary logistic model with slope 𝛃β;

  3. (coherence) the ordering constraint @eq-mlt-ordering reduces to θ1<⋯<θc−1 and so holds at every x at once;

  4. (interpretation) for any two regressor vectors and every r, 𝛃odds(Y>r∣x2)odds(Y>r∣x1)=exp⁡{(x2−x1)⊤β},{#eq-mlt-common-or}

    a single odds ratio that does not depend on r; and if 𝛃(x2−x1)⊤β>0 then the response at x2 is stochastically larger than the response at x1.

thm-mlt-score.title: Score, information and concavity
thm-mlt-score.html:
Under @def-mlt-baseline the log-likelihood, as a function of 𝛃𝛃𝛃β=(β1⊤,…,βc−1⊤)⊤, is 𝛃𝛃𝛈𝛃ℓ(β)=∑i=1n{∑r<cyirx(i)⊤βr−mib(ηi)},ηir=x(i)⊤βr.

Then:

  1. the score has blocks 𝛃𝛍∂ℓ/∂βr=∑i(yir−miπir)x(i)=X⊤(yr−μr), where 𝛍μr is the vector with entries miπir;

  2. the observed and expected information coincide and have blocks X⊤WrsX with Wrs=diag{miπir(δrs−πis)}i=1n;

  3. ℓ is concave, and strictly concave when rank(X)=p; in that case it has at most one maximizer, and the maximizer, if it exists, is the unique solution of the likelihood equations 𝛍X⊤(yr−μr)=0 for r=1,…,c−1.
